import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Fill missing 'Sleep Disorder' values for visualization clarity
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('No Disorder')

# Split 'Blood Pressure' into 'Systolic' and 'Diastolic' numeric columns
df[['Systolic', 'Diastolic']] = df['Blood Pressure'].str.split('/', expand=True).astype(int)

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots for a professional look
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create a 2x2 subplot grid to display multiple relationships
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(18, 16))
fig.suptitle('Analysis of Sleep and Health Metrics', fontsize=24, weight='bold')

# Define a color palette for consistent categorical coloring
palette = sns.color_palette("viridis", n_colors=df['BMI Category'].nunique())

# Plot 1: Sleep Duration vs. Stress Level, colored by Sleep Disorder
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Stress Level',
    y='Sleep Duration',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',
    style='BMI Category',
    s=250,
    ax=axes[0, 0],
    palette='magma'
)
axes[0, 0].set_title('Stress and BMI Impact on Sleep Duration', fontsize=16)
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Stress Level (1-10)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].legend(title='Condition')

# Plot 2: Physical Activity vs. Quality of Sleep, with point size by Daily Steps
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Physical Activity Level',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='BMI Category',
    size='Daily Steps',
    sizes=(150, 500),
    ax=axes[0, 1],
    palette=palette
)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Activity Level vs. Sleep Quality', fontsize=16)
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Physical Activity (minutes/day)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].legend(title='BMI & Steps')

# Plot 3: Blood Pressure Analysis with clinical reference lines
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Systolic',
    y='Diastolic',
    hue='BMI Category',
    s=250,
    ax=axes[1, 0],
    palette=palette
)
axes[1, 0].set_title('Blood Pressure by BMI Category', fontsize=16)
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Systolic Pressure (mmHg)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Diastolic Pressure (mmHg)', fontsize=12)
# Add reference lines for hypertension stage 1
axes[1, 0].axvline(130, color='orange', linestyle='--', lw=2, label='High BP Systolic (130)')
axes[1, 0].axhline(80, color='red', linestyle='--', lw=2, label='High BP Diastolic (80)')
axes[1, 0].legend()

# Plot 4: Relationship between Daily Steps and Heart Rate
sns.regplot(
    data=df,
    x='Daily Steps',
    y='Heart Rate',
    ax=axes[1, 1],
    scatter_kws={'s': 150, 'color': 'darkcyan'},
    line_kws={'color': 'red', 'lw': 2.5}
)
axes[1, 1].set_title('Heart Rate vs. Daily Steps', fontsize=16)
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Daily Steps', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Heart Rate (bpm)', fontsize=12)

# Adjust layout to prevent titles/labels from overlapping and save the figure
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close(fig)
